open_points.subject: open_store
open_points.text: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;
open_points.other_text: Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
open_points.question: Must a missing database path be accepted so the module can create the database, or must os.lstat successfully find an existing non-symbolic-link database before it is opened?

open_points.subject: record_change path policy and open_store database opening
open_points.text: Every file and directory the module itself opens under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links, by os.O_NOFOLLOW on each open;
open_points.other_text: the database file and its journal, which sqlite3 opens and cannot be told to refuse a link, are covered by open_store's walk before the connection opens and by the directory's privacy after;
open_points.question: Are the database file and journal exceptions to the requirement that every open use os.O_NOFOLLOW, or must their opens also satisfy that universal requirement?
